sources.title: 8.2 The Light-Dependent Reactions of Photosynthesis
notes: Chlorophyll a and b absorb different parts of visible spectrum, especially blue and red; green is comparatively reflected or transmitted.
Carotenoids broaden light capture and can protect photosynthetic machinery from excess energy.
Photosystems convert absorbed light into chemical-energy carriers.
sources.apa: OpenStax. (n.d.). 8.2 The Light-Dependent Reactions of Photosynthesis. https://openstax.org/books/biology/pages/8-2-the-light-dependent-reactions-of-photosynthesis

sources.title: 5.1 Overview of Photosynthesis
notes: Plant chlorophyll is embedded in thylakoid membranes inside chloroplasts.
Photosynthesis uses light, water and carbon dioxide to produce carbohydrates and release oxygen.

sources.title: Reflected Near-Infrared Waves
notes: Leaf pigments reflect green wavelengths; healthy vegetation also has a distinctive near-infrared response.
Remote sensors can detect visible and near-infrared vegetation signals.

sources.title: From Green to Brown
notes: Chlorophyll production and breakdown influence visible leaf color.
When chlorophyll declines, other pigments become more apparent.
sources.apa: NASA Earth Observatory. (n.d.). From Green to Brown. https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/from-green-to-brown-79332/

sources.title: How to Interpret a False-Color Satellite Image
notes: Plant chlorophyll has a recognizable spectral signature, absorbing red and blue and reflecting green.
False-color imaging can map vegetation using near-infrared reflection.
sources.apa: NASA Earth Observatory. (n.d.). How to Interpret a False-Color Satellite Image. https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/how-to-interpret-a-false-color-satellite-image/
